Rattled: You catch a glimpse of something in the Warp that sends shivers down your spine. Gain the @UUID[JournalEntry.DjxnvYJajGflu7IY.JournalEntryPage.Tu0sU1bo9eZI6qoe#frightened]{Frightened (Minor)} Condition.
Gritted Teeth: The power surges through you, and you suffer 3 Wounds.

Psychic Discharge: Any powered devices on your person, such as lasgun clips, dataslates, and vox-casters immediately lose their charge. You must recharge or repair these before they can be used again.

Warplight Cascade: Power gushes from you in arcs of iridescent light. All other characters within Short Range suffer a hit that deals [[1d10+6]] Damage. Targets may attempt to Dodge this hit as if it were a Ranged Attack with 1 SL.
Backlash: A violent burst of energy from the warp smashes your mind and you are sent reeling. You are @UUID[JournalEntry.DjxnvYJajGflu7IY.JournalEntryPage.Tu0sU1bo9eZI6qoe#stunned]{Stunned}.
Stolen Tongue: The capricious whims of the warp rob you of the ability to speak for [[1d10]] hours.

Photosensitivity: For [[1d10]] hours you become incredibly sensitive to light. You can see easily in almost pitch darkness. You do not suffer the effects of @UUID[JournalEntry.hdElQAwiBr5AyoRf.JournalEntryPage.zQYkbNcsJmGintdL#obscured]{Obscured} or @UUID[JournalEntry.hdElQAwiBr5AyoRf.JournalEntryPage.zQYkbNcsJmGintdL#poorly-lit]{Poorly Lit} environments, but you are @UUID[JournalEntry.DjxnvYJajGflu7IY.JournalEntryPage.Tu0sU1bo9eZI6qoe#blinded]{Blinded} while in Zones without those Traits exposed to bright light.
Feature Creep: Some element of your appearance — your eye or hair colour, your height, or your gait, changes subtly and permanently. The details of this are up to the GM.

Gibbering Wreck: You scream in pain as terrible insights from the Warp twist your mind. You are @UUID[JournalEntry.DjxnvYJajGflu7IY.JournalEntryPage.Tu0sU1bo9eZI6qoe#stunned]{Stunned} and exposed to a source of @UUID[JournalEntry.hdElQAwiBr5AyoRf.JournalEntryPage.PuzopCeKzYgcYAwh#moderate-exposure]{moderate Corruption}.
Soul Sear: Warp power courses through your body, leaving a permanent scar on your soul. For the next [[1d10]] hours you may not use any Psychic Powers.
Locked In: Warp energy floods your body, making it almost impossible to control. You are Restrained by an invisible force with Strength 50 for [[1d10]] rounds.

Concussive Blast: With an explosive crack of power you are rendered Unconscious. Characters in Short Range must pass a Challenging (+0) Fortitude (Endurance) Test or be @UUID[JournalEntry.DjxnvYJajGflu7IY.JournalEntryPage.Tu0sU1bo9eZI6qoe#stunned]{Stunned}.

Blood Rain: An unnatural psychic storm erupts, covering your Zone with a downpour of blood. In addition to this distressing effect, all Psychic Powers have their Warp Charge rating doubled if used inside this area.
Timeslip: Time flows oddly around you, and you are flung [[1d10]] rounds into the future. From everyone else’s point of view you simply disappear for [[1d10]] rounds.

Daemonic Emergence: A daemon tears its way out of the Warp and emerges within Short Range of you. Roll a d10 to determine what kind of daemon appears: 1-3, a @UUID[Compendium.apex-imperialis.navis-core-actors.Actor.4bhFOh1nTrYloc8s]{Plaguebearer}, 4-6, a @UUID[Compendium.apex-imperialis.navis-core-actors.Actor.r38KjnD2RWhYIykh]{Bloodletter}, 7-8 a @UUID[Compendium.apex-imperialis.navis-core-actors.Actor.xzqdh2P5F2c7QpVm]{Daemonette}, or a @UUID[Compendium.apex-imperialis.navis-core-actors.Actor.CAvzgSBWrbnHu8zi]{Pink Horror} appears.

Cataclysmic Blast: Power erupts forth from you in great arcs of coruscating energy. You and all other characters within Short Range suffer a hit that deals 3d10 Energy Damage. Additionally, all of your gear is destroyed on the spot, leaving you standing in a smoking crater.

Mass Possession: You scream in an unnatural, heretical tongue as daemonic entities attempt to use you as a bridge to enter the material universe. Roll a d10 at the beginning of each of your Turns — on a roll of 8 or more the effect ends. While the effect is in progress, you cannot Move and must spend your Action attempting to hold back the daemonic horde. You are a source of moderate Corruption while this effect persists.

Daemonhost: You must immediately pass a Very Hard (–30) Discipline Test or be possessed by a daemon. The details of this remain up to the GM, but it is almost certain that the being will attack all those around it regardless of their relationship to you. While you are most likely effectively dead, destruction of the Daemonhost may free your soul, if not save your life.

Eye of Terror: A substantial gate to the immaterium opens, and something truly terrible emerges. The nature of this remains up to the GM, but a Greater Daemon stepping through or an ancient Space Hulk appearing in orbit would be appropriate.

Hoarfrost: The area is covered with a thin layer of frost. Breath fogs in the air, and an unnatural chill infiltrates past even the thickest clothing and armour.

Lingering: The effect becomes permanent. The area can be heated temporarily by a huge expenditure of heat and energy, but eventually entropy and the chill of the grave reclaims it.

Banshee Howl: Loud screeching fills the area, periodically making it impossible to hear other sounds.

Lingering: Deafening screeches occur daily. The voice seems familiar to all who hear it.

Bloody Tears: Images such as pictures, icons and statues in the area appear to weep blood.

Lingering: The weeping becomes permanent. Any who drink the viscous blood dream of terrible portents.

Breath Leech: The air is sucked from the lungs of everyone present. Characters in your Zone must succeed at a Challenging (+0) Fortitude (Endurance) Test or become @UUID[JournalEntry.DjxnvYJajGflu7IY.JournalEntryPage.Tu0sU1bo9eZI6qoe#stunned]{Stunned} for one round.

Lingering: The air becomes permanently stale and difficult to breathe. Treat the Zone as though it were under the permanent influence of a @UUID[Compendium.apex-imperialis.navis-core-items.Item.OjLq7yDUPG8TpISi]{Choke Grenade}.

Dark Foreboding: An whispering breeze fills the area, giving those nearby a feeling of nameless dread.

Lingering: The area becomes permanently unsettling. Characters entering the Zone must make a Challenging (+0) Discipline (Fear) Test or become Frightened.

Distorted Reflection: Reflective surfaces in the area distort whatever they reflect, showing a twisted and disturbing version of reality.

Lingering: Surfaces in the area never quite reflect what is truly present. Individuals may draw unholy inspiration from the strange images they perceive.

Falling Upwards: Gravity reverses for a few seconds. Characters in your Zone must succeed at a Challenging (+0) Reflexes (Acrobatics) Test or suffer a 10 metre fall.

Lingering: Gravity permanently shifts in the area. Unnaturally high gravity inflicts the @UUID[JournalEntry.DjxnvYJajGflu7IY.JournalEntryPage.Tu0sU1bo9eZI6qoe#overburdened]{Overburdened} condition one anyone in the Zone. Occasionally gravity reverses without warning, as for Falling Upwards above.

Grave Chill: Nearby surfaces become cold to the touch, and breath fogs in the air.

Lingering: The area remains frigid in spite of attempts to warm it, and counts as a @UUID[JournalEntry.hdElQAwiBr5AyoRf.JournalEntryPage.UaRHLqZ99zmg7AeE#exposure]{Cold environment}.

Memory Worm: Everyone in the area finds it difficult to recall minor things such as people’s names or the time.

Lingering: The area becomes a permanent place of forgetfulness. It is difficult to recall most facts when in the area, and spending more than an hour there causes someone to forget something substantial.

Mounting Paranoia: Everyone in the area has the sudden unshakeable sensation that they are being watched.

Lingering: The area becomes mired in a permanent aura of mistrust and paranoia. Anyone spending more than an hour in the area begins to suspect everyone around them of malign intent.

Rot and Decay: Any perishable goods in the area become stale and unpalatable, and insects and small animals nearby quickly perish.

Lingering: The area gains a permanent faint smell of lingering rot. Living plants, small creatures, and foodstuffs all perish or decay here in hours, and new diseases crop up frequently in the surrounding area.

Veil of Darkness: All light sources dim substantially, causing the Zone to become @UUID[JournalEntry.hdElQAwiBr5AyoRf.JournalEntryPage.zQYkbNcsJmGintdL#poorly-lit]{Poorly Lit}.

Lingering: The effect becomes permanent.

Warp Echoes: Everyone in the Zone hears echoing voices and sounds from past events and things yet to be. Characters who hear this bewildering cacophony must pass a Challenging (+0) Discipline Test or be @UUID[JournalEntry.DjxnvYJajGflu7IY.JournalEntryPage.Tu0sU1bo9eZI6qoe#stunned]{Stunned}.

Lingering: Whispering and distant voices haunt the Zone forever. They may mislead or inform listeners.
Psychic Breakthrough: Roll again on this table, rerolling results of 101+, and apply both the standard and Lingering effect of that result.

Perils of the Warp: Something has gone terribly wrong. Roll again on the @UUID[RollTable.2YYlAUyaVIt4bZVa]{Perils of the Warp} Table, exactly as if you had failed a test to control your accumulated Warp Charge.

You fall to the bottom of the Initiative order on the next Round.

You flounder clumsily as you attack, knocking you precariously off balance.

You have Disadvantage on all Tests until the end of your next turn.

A poorly controlled swing or shot causes you to lurch and drop your weapon.

You drop the weapon you used to attack. Anyone can pick it up with a Free Action.

You stumble due to an unwieldy swing or unexpected recoil.

You fall @UUID[JournalEntry.DjxnvYJajGflu7IY.JournalEntryPage.Tu0sU1bo9eZI6qoe#prone]{Prone}.

Your reckless attack causes you to twist your ankle, either by overextending in melee or buckling when absorbing recoil.

Your Speed is reduced to Slow until the end of the current encounter. This does not count as a Critical Wound.

You mishandle your weapon, striking it on a hard surface or interfering with the workings of its Machine Spirit.

Your weapon is @UUID[JournalEntry.wqlquQ8Njtd5fb4Y.JournalEntryPage.wsM53RDPPrqwS3Te#unstable]{Unstable} until it is fixed with a Hard (-20) Tech (Engineering) Test.

Your ungainly attack manages to briefly blind or deafen you. Perhaps you overloaded a plasma weapon, causing a searing burst of light, used a Loud weapon too close to your ear, or clumsily struck your own eye when your attack ricochetted.

You are @UUID[JournalEntry.DjxnvYJajGflu7IY.JournalEntryPage.Tu0sU1bo9eZI6qoe#blinded]{Blinded} or @UUID[JournalEntry.DjxnvYJajGflu7IY.JournalEntryPage.Tu0sU1bo9eZI6qoe#deafened]{Deafened}, whichever is determined more appropriate for your weapon by the GM.

Your graceless attack causes minor damage to your protective gear.

Your Armour in a random hit location is reduced by 1 until repaired (see @UUID[JournalEntry.J8NVn5iNgM57cKmw.JournalEntryPage.NrJuy93Put0XCYq9#tech-(int)]{Tech}). If you aren't wearing any armour in that location, you suffer 1 Wound instead.

In the fumbling confusion of battle, you manage to clumsily strike yourself with a glancing blow. You are either @UUID[JournalEntry.DjxnvYJajGflu7IY.JournalEntryPage.Tu0sU1bo9eZI6qoe#stunned]{Stunned} or @UUID[JournalEntry.DjxnvYJajGflu7IY.JournalEntryPage.Tu0sU1bo9eZI6qoe#bleeding]{Bleeding}, whichever is determined more appropriate for your weapon by the GM.

Your attack hits an unintended target. If you roll this Fumble on a successful attack, your melee weapon might cleave through an enemy and into an ally, or a bullet might ricochet after passing through a foe.

Your attack hits a random ally within weapon range with +0 SL. Roll to determine a random hit location. If there is no target in range, you somehow hit yourself.

Arrested: A member of your party has been accused of a grave crime and arrested when they least expect it. They may be accused of murder, heresy, or worse still, evading Imperial tithes and levies. Any other character can spend an Endeavour to attempt to prove their ally’s innocence with an Routine (+20) Lore Test. Otherwise, the party must spend an additional two Endeavours to free them (by the proper channels or otherwise). Alternatively, the party’s Patron will intervene to free the Character, if only to ensure their own secrets are not spread. This reduces the Patron’s favour with whatever Faction imprisoned the Character by 1.

Chance Encounter: During your downtime, you happen upon an individual who holds strange or unique knowledge that might be of use to you in the future. The next time you take the Expert Advice Endeavour you count as having previously located an expert.

Argument: An encounter with a member of another Faction (use the @UUID[Compendium.apex-imperialis.navis-core-tables.RollTable.vl9saE1Hpu48qsLd]{Patron Faction} table to determine which). The encounter ends badly — perhaps you interrupt the vital work of a Tech-priest, or stumble into the midst of a Infractionist’s illegal dealings. You escape with your life, but that individual bears a lasting grudge against you. The effects of this are left up to the GM.

Death in the Shadows: An allied NPC has a close brush with death, and turns to you for help. You may spend an Endeavour to assist them in some way — strengthening their security, tracking down an attacker, or otherwise working to prevent their death. If you fail to do so your ally develops a grudge against you, or may even turn up dead!

Hunted: You realise you are being followed! This goes on for days, with your pursuers always staying one step ahead of any attempt to confront them. They may be Vigilites who suspect you of some crime, Infractionists who seek to blackmail you, or even other agents of your Patron watching for disloyalty. The paranoia makes it difficult to rest, and you begin your next mission @UUID[JournalEntry.DjxnvYJajGflu7IY.JournalEntryPage.Tu0sU1bo9eZI6qoe#fatigued]{Fatigued}.

Riots: Agitators have ignited a full blown riot among the local citizenry. Perhaps a contaminated shipment of Grey Rations has led to rumours of food shortages, a popular local preacher was censured for heresy by the Adeptus Ministorum, or the Character’s own actions have spurred violence! Due to the disruption, all Tests made to complete Endeavours during the subsequent Downtime period suffer −2 SL.

Contagion: A plague is sweeping through the area, perhaps Uhlren's Pox or even a limited outbreak of the lethal Creeping Blight. Make a Difficult (−10) Resilience Test. If you fail, you contract a disease and begin your next mission @UUID[JournalEntry.DjxnvYJajGflu7IY.JournalEntryPage.Tu0sU1bo9eZI6qoe#poisoned]{Poisoned}. To heal the disease and remove the Poisoned Condition, you must receive adequate medicae treatment (as the GM determines).

Crackdown: The local authorities have declared a lockdown. Vigilites may patrol the streets in search of known infractionists, or Skittari Vanguard be searching the slums of a Forge World to round up volunteers for the next tithe. The party has Disadvantage on all Tests to undertake illicit activity or Endeavours during this downtime.

Displeased Machine Spirit: An item of equipment you own falls into disrepair and frustrates attempts to fix it. It is up to the GM to decide which piece of equipment this is, though it should be something reasonably expensive or important to the character. See @UUID[JournalEntry.J8NVn5iNgM57cKmw.JournalEntryPage.NrJuy93Put0XCYq9#tech-(int)]{Tech} on repairing equipment.

Favours Repaid: Someone from your past takes the opportunity to return a significant favour. The precise nature of this service should depend on your previous missions and the NPCs you have assisted during your missions or previous life. Whatever it is, the NPC in question dearly wants to make good and is willing to help in a future Endeavour or mission.

Foreboding Vision: You are provided with a cryptic vision, perhaps in a dream, during a fervent prayer to the Emperor, or hidden in the midst of binharic emissions of a malfunctioning machine. You begin your next mission with one extra Fate point, in excess of your Fate value. Once spent, this bonus Fate point does not return.

Unexpected Gift: You receive an unexpected gift from an unknown benefactor. This is a piece of Common equipment selected by the GM, but it should be something useful to you. It may have been left in your quarters while you were absent, shoved into your hands by a passing stranger who vanishes into the crowd, or simply assigned to you years ago by the byzantine bureaucracy of the Adeptus Administratum. It is up to the GM who is responsible for this largesse, and if they expect anything in return.

Languishing Patron: This Event may only occur once during a period of downtime. If multiple Characters generate this Event it still only occurs once.

Powerful and wealthy as Patrons are, even they are not immortal. During the period of downtime your Patron suffers a serious misfortune. Maybe this is a social or political humiliation, their health deteriorates, or they suffer an injury. The first time this result is generated on the Events Table the GM should make a note of it and decide whether the Patron has suffered a fall from grace or serious injury. If the Patron has been humiliated, they reduce their Influence score by 1 with a relevant faction. If the Patron is injured, there is no immediate consequence, though the Characters may come to learn of it and it may impact their ability to communicate with and ask assistance of their Patron.

Bounty Hunter: Word reaches you that a bounty has been put out on your head. Maybe you inadvertently killed or angered the wrong person in your previous mission, or a rival has simply grown tired of your interference. Whatever the cause, a @UUID[Compendium.apex-imperialis.navis-core-actors.Actor.5CCbRXAMBtwviuFE]{Bounty Hunter} has been set on your tail. For now, there is no effect, but at some inconvenient point in a future mission the Bounty Hunter will appear to claim you. If at any point at least half the Characters in the party are being pursued by Bounty Hunters, they will band together into a Venator gang and hunt the entire party instead.

Obligations: Someone who once did you a favour returns to collect on it. Perhaps they are a Macharian Vigilite who overlooked a minor infraction, an Administratum adept who expedited some vital request, or an old Astra Militarum comrade who saved your life. They request something substantial of you that is neither simple to provide nor easy to dismiss. This could involve multiple Endeavours to resolve, or even form the basis of a future mission. The details are up to the GM.

Unmissable Opportunity: The chance to make a few easy solars presents itself. Maybe you win a high stakes game of Regicide, or a desperate citizen offers you a small fortune for your urgent assistance. If you go on to make a successful Income Endeavour during this downtime, double any earnings you make.

Victory Celebration: A great celebration takes place! Perhaps it marks the day Saint Macharius’s forces liberated the world and returned it to the Emperor’s embrace, or perhaps it is an ancient local celebration whose origins are lost to time. Regardless it offers a momentary respite from the endless toil and misery of life in the Imperium. Characters who choose to take part in the celebration feel rested and rejuvenated, and may ignore the next @UUID[JournalEntry.DjxnvYJajGflu7IY.JournalEntryPage.Tu0sU1bo9eZI6qoe#fatigued]{Fatigued} Condition they acquire.

Crushing Tithe: Conflict breaks out in a nearby sub-sector and the Imperial tithes are raised in its defence. The party lose 50% of all their accumulated wealth that hasn’t been stashed or invested with the Speculation Endeavour. Alternatively, each party member must surrender a Common or Rare weapon to the cause instead.

A Very Important Visitor: You cross paths with a very important individual. Perhaps an agri world is being visited by a senior member of the Administratum, an orbital plays host to a wealthy Rogue Trader, or the workings of an Forge world are personally inspected by a Magos Dominus. You may choose to make a Very Hard (−30) Social Test. If successful, you manage to impress them — you gain +1 Influence with that Faction, to a maximum of +2. If you fail, your influence falls by 1 instead.

rows.text: You wish to track the source of a particular line of trade in xenos weaponry and unearth the secrets at its roots, dismantling all access to the heretical artefacts that have continued to cross your path.
You are committed to uncovering the long-rumoured heresies whispered to hide within a noble house, despite the failure of all who tried before you.
You aim to gather enough data to write a treatise on the cults of a specific Chaos God within the sector, gaining the attention and influence of your Holy Order.
You strive to hunt and destroy a daemonic entity that has eluded you throughout many investigations and missions. You seek knowledge that will finally allow you to succeed.
You are confident you deserve promotion to Interrogator and manoeuvre to ensure the less-than-righteous circumstances of your formative years do not impede this eventuality.

You have committed grave sins against the God-Emperor. You seek to destroy and silence all evidence of your wrongdoings or repent so sufficiently via deed and service that your weakness is never uncovered.

You are unsure about various points of doctrine within the Imperial cult as you have been taught to practise it. You seek evidence that can prove the purest methods for living for the glory of the God-Emperor.

You have a vicious past with a specific subgroup of Macharian xenos or cultists. Perhaps they are centralised on one world and sprawl throughout the system. Regardless, you will not move on until they are scoured from existence.

You are devoted to the death of a specific Chaos or xenos entity responsible for the many scars you bear on your body and psyche. All other heresy you dismantle is a convenient dress rehearsal for your eventual vengeance.

You have witnessed a highly-respected Inquisitor’s ongoing descent into increasingly explicit heresy. It is perilous to accuse them without sufficient void-tight evidence, but you vow to eventually bring them to justice.

The Rosette is trapped with a @UUID[Compendium.apex-imperialis.navis-core-items.Item.99dVOsy85KLNtGTj]{Melta Bomb}, which is triggered whenever it is handled by an individual who the Inquisitor has not sanctioned.

The Rosette contains an emergency distress beacon that emits a homing signal. It broadcasts its location through coded communication only discernable by Inquisition-controlled vox channels. Its range extends to the area of a planet

The Rosette has an emergency trigger that can be activated as a Free Action and functions as a @UUID[Compendium.apex-imperialis.navis-core-items.Item.kw9N0gOOA3YVqN4i]{Smoke Grenade}, a @UUID[Compendium.apex-imperialis.navis-core-items.Item.deHQEH976yh9nI9y]{Signal Jammer}, and a @UUID[Compendium.apex-imperialis.navis-core-items.Item.V2OgwHeEr3qpTbBy]{Stummer} simultaneously.

An abandoned Arbites or Vigilite watch post complete with a guard tower. There are some lockers within containing old uniforms and odd pieces of equipment.
An ancillary hangar unit attached to the local voidport. It is large enough to base a Valkyrie or similar vehicle and is close to local and offworld transportation hubs.
The basement of a run-down bar owned by an infractionist gang. Has a secluded service entrance. Characters can work the bar above to gather intel and solidify their cover identities.
An empty wing of a noble’s mansion, complete with secret entrances and exits. The noble of the house is a sour fellow who dislikes the presence of the characters despite owing their Patron dearly.

The uppermost floors of an abandoned hive spire, containing floors of dusty apartments, meeting halls, and viewing platforms. A hidden elevator leads to the hive below; otherwise, it is a long way down.

An unused corner of a manufatorum, set aside by a local Tech-Priest for Inquisition use. It has a surplus of essential tools and materials, and the surrounding industrial ambience can obscure loud activities.

A seldom visited wing of an Administratum archivium, filled with ancient and dusty tithe records. Characters on good terms with the Administratum can access local information easily from adjacent wings.

A small but well-maintained cathedrum. The small Imperial Cult attached to the cathedrum is a carefully devised front — but the priests within are still devout and have been told to stay away from the characters and treat them as if they were saints.
The Rosette is hard-wired with archaic translation technologies, allowing its user to make a Linguistics (Forbidden) Test with Advantage once per day.

The Rosette incorporates an anachronistic system of scanners that can determine the provenance of a piece of technology. A character can make a Difficult (−10) Tech Test to determine whether or not a xenos species may have constructed the tech.

The rosette bears Jokaero modifications, including a digi-laser set into it for the Inquisitor to use as a last resort. The rosette acts as a Laspistol, in which the Magazine automatically regenerates fully 24 hours after firing, fed by a Jokaero-crafted power source.

The Rosette can be activated to emit a highpitched debilitating screech only discernable by a particular xenos species within Medium Range (choose from Aeldari and Drukhari,Orks, T’au, or Kroot). Characters affected by this shrill noise must make a Difficult (−10) Fortitude (Endurance) Test or become Deafened and Stunned for 3 Rounds.

It's All Over Me!: The character is overcome by their hallucination, believing bugs or rats are swarming them or that their body is melting or ablaze, and counts as being @UUID[Compendium.apex-imperialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.DjxnvYJajGflu7IY.JournalEntryPage.Tu0sU1bo9eZI6qoe#stunned]{Stunned} for the duration.

Lost in the Void / The Emperor’s Light!: The character believes they are consumed by darkness or lost in a blinding flash of unnatural light for the duration. The character acts as if @UUID[Compendium.apex-imperialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.DjxnvYJajGflu7IY.JournalEntryPage.Tu0sU1bo9eZI6qoe#blinded]{Blinded}.
I’m Sinking!: The character believes the floor is obstructed by rubble or melting, and they are desperately trying to escape. The character’s Speed becomes Slow for the duration.

Something In The Walls: The character perceives horrifying creatures coming out of the walls or bursting out of the ground and attacks them in random directions for the duration. Randomly determine the direction of their attack, and if there are any creatures in that line of fire, randomly determine one to be the target.

Trapped In A Maze: The character thinks that the battlefield has shifted, such that new barriers have fallen into place, or perhaps they have wandered into an elaborate trap. The character cannot leave their current Zone for the duration, believing there are impassable barriers surrounding them.
The Inquisitor uses a relay of astropaths and psykers to mentally transmit orders to one of their acolytes, rendering them incapacitated until they finish delivering the message on their behalf.
The Inquisitor uses Infractionist couriers to relay messages: well paid, sufficiently threatened and blackmailed individuals who fear their wrath.
The Inquisitor broadcasts book cyphers on a local vox system — the characters need to use the contents of a particular local archivium to decode each message.
The Inquisitor plants encoded messages into the sermons of local preachers. The characters need to attend each daily service to ensure they receive new messages.
The Inquisitor hides written orders packed within the bullet casings of munition shipments sent to their acolytes; each bullet is stamped with the Inquisition’s mark.
Through means unknown to the characters, the Inquisitor hijacks servo skulls in local service and re-directs them to deliver and retrieve messages from them.

The Inquisitor uses polymorphine — on themselves or designated messengers — to issue commands behind the faces of the local populace, identifying themself using a signet ring resembling their rosette.

The Inquisitor’s messages are delivered by a cyber-familliar bird of prey with bladed wings and numerous augmetics, including a hololithic projector installed in a second mechanical head that relays the Inquisitor’s orders visually.

The Inquisitor uses a rotating schedule of encrypted vox channels. Characters are expected to know the mathematics and cyphers to use the correct channel and check in at the correctly scheduled times.

The Inquisitor assigns a servitor to the characters that broadcasts Imperial hymns to ensure they keep true to their faith. In reality, it broadcasts messages through coded interference to the signal, producing sounds that others can only identify as a cacophony.

Silent Traders: Strange dealings in the markets suggest the possibility that a dealer in proscribed alien goods has been set up nearby. Until the next downtime period, the character who overheard these dealings may attempt to find Exotic goods of xenos origin as if they were Rare. However, failing the Availability Test panics the vendor into leaving and may result in additional reprisal.

Odd Fellow: A stranger glimpsed through a crowd has a strangely inhuman posture and movement — too still one moment, then impossibly swift and graceful the next. Choosing to follow this stranger begins a nighimpossible chase. Make a Hard (−20) Athletics (Running) Test; succeeding grants useful intel on the abnormal individual and opens new leads. Add +1 SL to any Tests to investigate xenos presence in the next mission.

Unwanted Nuisance: Xenos pests proliferate in the regions where the character spends their downtime, destroying supplies and becoming a general nuisance, if not a full-blown threat. The Availability of perishable goods and vulnerable machinery (as determined by the GM) is reduced by one step until the next downtime period. If this result occurs multiple times, it may indicate a permanent infestation that impacts a world until more serious action is taken.

Political Emergence: A rare authority such as a Rogue Trader is in the region, one with the political clout to challenge even the Holy Ordos — or to aid them. The character can track down rumours of their activities and curry favour within the visitor’s hierarchy to smooth upcoming Inquisitorial operations. To do this, the character makes a Challenging (+0) Rapport (Inquiry) Test. Succeeding, they treat their Influence with a Faction of their choice as being 1 higher until the next downtime period.

Emergency Task: The character receives a direct missive from their Inquisitor, instructing them to investigate a nearby matter instead of receiving the normal benefits of downtime. The GM should treat completing this task as a Challenging (−0) Extended Test using a Skill of their choice (defaulting to the character’s Skill with the highest chance of success if uncertain — their Inquisitor did not choose them on a whim!). The character may make three attempts to complete the task in time. For their efforts, they receive a bonus of 100 Solars per SL achieved at the beginning of their next downtime period in compensation for the time lost. They may receive recognition by other means for their sacrifices to be ever-ready for duty.

Sleepless Nights: Strange omens haunt the character’s dreams, portending possible daemonic activity. The character can make a Difficult (−10) Discipline (Psychic) Test to endure the bewildering nightmares and discover their hidden meanings. On a success, at any point before the next downtime period, the character may add +2 SL to a Test of their choice. On a failure, the character suffers a @Corruption[minor]{Minor Exposure} to @UUID[Compendium.apex-imperialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.hdElQAwiBr5AyoRf.JournalEntryPage.PuzopCeKzYgcYAwh]{Corruption}.

Fastidious Investigation: Rumours of daemons are usually just that, but vigilance demands investigation nonetheless. Dutifully scouring leads takes enough time to impose Disadvantage on any Tests made to complete Endeavours during this downtime period, but the character gains +1 temporary Influence with the Inquisition and the Adeptus Ministorum until their next downtime period.

Warp Portents: Techno-arcane readings suggest a thinning of realspace nearby. Although likely a temporary phenomenon with the potential to pass harmlessly, the risk of daemonic influence increases until the effect recedes. Any sources of Corruption the character experiences until their next downtime period inflict 1 additional Corruption when any is gained.

Corrupted Source: Supplies throughout the region have been contaminated by some unwholesome presence. Regardless of origin, relying on local provender risks exposure to the dangerous agent. The character may spend 1d10 × 50 Solars on imported supplies that can last until the contaminants are rooted out. If they do not, they must make a Difficult (−10) Fortitude (Endurance) or Fortitude (Poison) Test to either deal with privation or weather the effects of consuming the tainted supplies. Failing the Fortitude (Endurance) causes the character to begin their next mission Fatigued, while failing the Fortitude (Poison) Test inflicts 1 Corruption upon them.

Sabotage: Local manufactorum slowdowns have left vital goods in short supply, leading to hoarding by the authorities. The Inquisition has the right to claim their share of these goods, but doing so jeopardises immediate support. Until the character’s next downtime period, when attempting to acquire new items, prices are increased by 50%. The character can ignore this increase with an official requisition, but doing so decreases their Influence with local power structures by 1, or causes a decrease in @UUID[Compendium.apex-imperialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.KbejcPMug5gfoWWz.JournalEntryPage.XyTxLhjDZDkpE0Lz]{Subtlety} until the end of their next downtime.

Psyker Hunt: Hints of burgeoning psyker activity nearby demand attention. The character can browbeat answers out of the populace with a Challenging (+0) Presence (Intimidation) Test, investigate for the latent psyker with a Difficult (−10) Intuition (Surroundings) Test, or when all else fails, draw on their authority within the Ordos and organise a witch-hunt, requiring no Test but causing a decrease in their @UUID[Compendium.apex-imperialis.navis-inquisition-journals.JournalEntry.KbejcPMug5gfoWWz.JournalEntryPage.XyTxLhjDZDkpE0Lz]{Subtlety} Level. Success reveals the rogue psyker and captures them, turning them over to the authorities for containment until the Black Ships arrive and granting the character a temporary increase of +1 Influence with members of the Adeptus Astra Telepathica and the Inquisition until the character’s next downtime period.

Web of Lies: The populace is in a frenzy over suspected heresy and witchcraft, with gossips and info-brokers speaking of nothing but suspected culprits. Sifting through baseless rumours requires a Challenging (+0) Rapport (Inquiry) Test. Success grants +2 SL on a single roll of the character’s choice until their next downtime period, related to local happenings, known ne’er-do-wells and miscreants, and unusual phenomena in the area.

Sowed Fears: Recent witch-burnings, public excruciations, or other gruesome punishments have left the populace compliant for the moment, driving any unrest deeper underground. Until the next downtime period, making an official display of Inquisitorial authority grants the character +1 SL on relevant Tests. However, any failed Tests suffer an additional −2 SL, as the locals turn volatile and vent their frustrations on the character.
The Rosette features a sensitive psycho-active crystalline structure that vibrates and chimes ominously whenever realspace is breached by a Warp portal or a daemonic incursion within 1km.

The Rosette is covered in concealed hexagrammic wards. When a Psychic Power targets the bearer of the Rosette, they may present the Rosette to impose Disadvantage on the Psychic Mastery Test. The hexagrammic wards then briefly burn out and can be restored by spending an hour in meditation and devotion.

The Rosette is composed around a core similar to a Null Rod. This Rosette can be used as part of a melee attack against a target with a Warp Threshold. The attack gains Rend (X), where X is the current Warp Charge of the target. After this effect is used, it takes a week to recharge.

The Rosette incorporates a miniature Aurascrye, a rare and arcane piece of technology that operates similarly to an @UUID[Compendium.apex-imperialis.navis-core-items.Item.dO7XoDXD9QYTy6zZ]{Auspex} explicitly designed to detect the presence of daemons. It works for one hour before requiring a 12-hour recharge.

The Rosette is genuinely ancient and built around a miniaturised Geller Field generator. The Geller Field generator can be activated as an Action with a Very Hard (−30) Tech Test to protect the individual holding it for a number of hours equal to the SL from the effects of Perils of the Warp, Warp Phenomena, and Psychic Powers, or shunt them from the Warp into realspace. A high-ranking Magos of the Adeptus Mechanicus may be able to recharge this device after it has been used
A miasmic aura of choking smoke surrounds the blade, each strike trailing dark, foetid energy through the air.
The blade’s metal appears jagged and brittle, growing and reforming crystalline edges and jutting spikes before retracting and growing anew.
The blade is charred and blackened as if someone had attempted to destroy it with flames. The cracked and unnaturally blistered surface bleeds flames from some impossible depth.
The weapon rings with a strange and eerie resonance when drawn as if struck with a tuning fork. Each strike and cut with the blade causes it to howl through the air.
The blade is wreathed in cold, multi-hued flames. Though they give off no light, they paint the world in eerie and unnatural colours.
When drawn, the blade appears to pull at the light, dimming rooms and chambers, surrounding itself with a tainted miasma of light.
A baleful eye sits within the crossguard, and many teeth grow from the hilt, encircling the wielder’s hand in a none-too-subtle threat.
The blade is surrounded by silent, flickering arcs of warp lightning, charging the air with invisible but potent potential energy.
Covered in a sickly sheen, the blade leaks venom and sickness from pores and cracks, these droplets sizzle on contact with reality.
The blade possesses an unnaturally beatific sheen and warps light about itself, so it is impossible to tell which is the blade and which is an illusory shaft of light.
Conceited: The weapon conveys Disadvantage when attempting to Defend.
Intoxicating: The wielder has −1 SL to any Fortitude Test to resist drugs, gases, or poisons.
Overbearing: The weapon’s Encumbrance is increased by 1.
Punishing: When the wielder misses an attack, they immediately suffer 1 non-critical wound.
Untenable: When the wielder loses Influence with a Faction, roll 1d10. On a 5+, they lose 1 additional point of Influence.
The Rosette is made from silver and inlaid with circuitry akin to an electoo. When its Inquisitor engages its gene sensors, its circuitry shimmers.
The Rosette is made from vat-grown bone sourced from the Inquisitor's own DNA, naturally carrying their genetic marker.
The Rosette is composed of black marble, hewn into an icon of the Inquisition. It is perennially ice-cold to the touch but believed to burn the flesh of the impure.
The Rosette is hewn from the bone of a longforgotten Inquisitor Lord, intricately inlaid with polished silver shaped into an incomprehensible script and the symbol of the Inquisition.
The Rosette is composed of layers of damaged plasteel armour that reportedly belonged to a saint, salvaged from an ancient battlefield.

The Rosette is composed of a seemingly featureless slab of incredibly dense, unidentified metal. When its Inquisitor activates its gene lock, it projects a miniature hololithic image of their face and accompanying credentials.

The Rosette is composed of hardened glass and shaped into an hourglass filled with fine sand. High Gothic stricture debossed into the glass lists the names of the many Inquisitors that have used this Rosette in the past and proclaims that the sand within is from Holy Terra.
The Rosette is composed of battle-worn ceramite. Meticulous carvings tell grim tales of how its protection has saved the lives of its previous bearers.

The Rosette is composed of reclaimed rockcrete from the ruin of a cathedrum, the site of a battle against an enemy of the Holy Ordos. Shaped into a censer, its inner chamber partially filled with the Inquisitor’s cerebrospinal fluid to bear their unique genetic signature.

The Rosette is composed of densely layered purity seals, treated with potent lacquers to fuse them together. The conglomerate of scriptures seems to join together through fervid design or inconceivable coincidence, forming a disjointed orthopraxic hymn that lingers in the mind.

The Rosette is suffused with once-sanctioned psychic energy, which can be used as a Psy Focus and the wielder to make a Psyniscience Test with Advantage once per day

The Rosette incorporates the bones of a blank servant of the Inquisition. By spending a point of Fate to activate the Rosette, psykers within Medium Range must make a Difficult (−10) Discipline (Composure) Test or become visibly Stunned for the next 3 Rounds.

The Rosette is inscribed with archaic hexagrammic wards, capable of expediting the dissipation of psychic energy. Wielders can spend an action to immediately halve their current Warp Charge. These wards regain efficacy after one week.

The Rosette features cryptic technology that functions similarly to a Soulguilt Scanner. Once per day, the bearer can gain Advantage on an Awareness, Intuition, or Navigation Test to hunt heretics, rogue psykers, or mutants.
The Rosette is enmeshed with psycho-active materials similar to a Psyocculum, exhibiting barely detectable micro-vibrations when brought closer to a daemon or psyker within Medium Range.

rows.text: Loud: The function of this piece of equipment is very loud, and may draw the attention of onlookers when used.
Loathing Spirit: When you gain 1 or more Corruption, the next time you use this item, you must first pass a Challenging (+0) Tech Test or the equipment refuses to function and must be repaired.
Unorthodox: This piece of equipment will not function for the day, and will be considered broken, unless you perform a one-hour, unusual, and suspicious ritual to appease it.

Repugnant Spirit: Once per encounter, when you use this item and have a Malignancy or Mutation, you must roll on the @UUID[Compendium.apex-imperialis.navis-core-tables.RollTable.HL6DtTGWIUQy5NZ9]{Fumble} Table.
Bellicose Design: The item has garnered an offensive or distasteful appearance or function for one of the Factions of the Imperium, and they are likely to have a negative disposition toward you.
Unclean: This equipment is difficult to keep clean and attracts filth and contamination from various environments.
Inauspicious: When you Spend Fate or Burn Fate, the next time you use this item, you must first pass a Challenging (+0) Tech Test or the equipment ceases to function and must be repaired.

Immaterial Abhorrence: Once per encounter, in the presence of a daemon or creature with a Warp Threshold, you must succeed on a Challenging (+0) Tech Test or the equipment ceases to function and must be repaired.
Prone to Mishap: This equipment or item is quick to take damage, bears it poorly, and may take longer to repair than other items.
Cascading Defeat: Once per encounter, when you fail a Test related to the equipment being used or while using that equipment, it ceases to function and must be repaired before being used again.
Hull Wretches: Even the society within a voidship has room to leave forgotten dregs, beggars, and pickpockets making their dwellings in the rusted hollows beneath fuel lines and cargo holds.

Maintenance Servitors: Programming overrides thoughts, denying them any expression of their silent agony as they move through the vessel on clanging steps to fasten rivets, clean floors, and oil bulkheads.
Lower Deck Voidsmen: Oil-stained jumpsuits, lamp skinplants, and scars of machine accidents mark them as those who seek and repair malfunctions in the ship’s bowels.

Penal Regiment: The cargo hold mills with warriors in flimsy armour, numbered jumpsuits, and collars with blinking lights, their separation from the crew maintained by armed officers and the ship’s armsmen.
Macharian Pilgrims: For them, this vessel is just a small leg of a decades-long journey. The ragged and pious sing hymns of their homeworld and offer blessings to passengers and crew.
Voidsmen Engineers: A cadre of crew dressed in voidsuits moves through the corridors. The shift has changed, and it is their turn to brave the void on external repair duty.
Astra Militarum Troopers: Well drilled in the presence of their officers, rowdy in their downtime; the corridors ring with marching boots, barked orders, and the murmur of conversation.
Main Deck Voidsmen: The crew perform menial duties, moving cargo, taking readings from gauges on pipework, and occasionally relaying vox messages to other parts of the ship.

Cargo Pilots: The hold is loaded with Departmento Munitorum cargo containers and @UUID[Compendium.apex-imperialis.navis-requisition-actors.Actor.SSqyPXq4qRxqxFFu]{Arvus Lighters}. Their pilots share lho sticks and recaff, relishing the quiet before they reach port.
Armsmen: In clean Navy uniforms or bearing the captain’s livery, they patrol the decks, discussing their last combat — a bloody defence against an enemy boarding action.
Tech-Priest: The red-robed servant of the Omnissiah spreads holy unguents from a censer as they wander the corridors, overseeing complex maintenance procedures and soothing the vessel’s spirit.
Ministorum Priest: The ship is their cathedral, their faith is the light the crew turns to in their darkest moments. They tend to the voidship’s shrines and host regular sermons.
Silent Traders: Merchants dressed in brocaded voidsuits oversee the movement of a heavily guarded cargo cache and offer surreptitious payments to the crew and captain to keep quiet.
Highborn Scions: With the freedom their position affords them, they travel in luxury cabins and dine with the captain, dressed in the finery of their homeworlds.
Rogue Trader and Retinue: A dashing scoundrel and their associates are capering about aboard, gambling and drinking with those aboard, and causing trouble for the crew.

Adeptus Administratum Logistics Inspectors: They seek to rectify a tithe discrepancy at the next port, their fingers ever-tapping on dataslates, a scrivener servitor whirring as it records their every word.
Senior Officer: A member of the bridge crew and a retinue of armsmen travel the corridors on an essential matter for the vessel’s security; voidsmen salute them as they pass.
Adepta Sororitas: A group of sisters from one of the holy orders, bearing the flame of the Emperor’s light to the vessel’s destination.
Captain: Escorted by armsmen, the captain guides a guest through the vessel’s corridors, proudly discussing the intertwined histories of the voidship and their family.
Space Marine: The crew speak in hushed murmurs of a lone traveller in power armour sequestered aboard their vessel. An angel of death walks among them.
When the engine roars, stamp your foot thrice on the deck to return the machine spirit’s call.
Offer prayer only at the vessel’s heart, for Terra is the heart of the Imperium.
By emergency light or candle, allow no deck to fall into shadow.
All who board must carve their name into the hull so the vessel’s spirit will know them.
Make the sign of the Aquila the first time you hear the ship’s guns fire.
All oaths made aboard the voidship are sworn in the names of the Emperor and the captain.
The internal bulkheads are left open to allow the vessel’s spirit freedom of passage.
The voidship must not be renamed, for the Emperor would not know it by its new name, and He would lose sight of it.
Any canid aboard tempts ill fortune, for the howling tumult of Warp calls to it, urging it to howl back.
Unused corridors and cabins are left in darkness as sanctuaries for the souls of those who have died aboard.
Refrain from singing whilst travelling the Warp. Risk not impeding the Astronomican’s chorus.
A day’s rations thrown into the darkness below decks alleviates ill fortune, provided no impact sound is heard.
When praying, touch the voidship’s structure barehanded, that the machine spirit will hear thee and amplify thy prayers.
Drum twice on the bulkhead before entering a lightless corridor, but do not enter if a response sounds.
Toenail clippings left against the ship’s bulkheads strengthen the bolts and rivets holding them together.
When first experiencing Warp travel, new crew members must wear blindfolds on their first day in the Warp.
Those who die aboard must remain aboard; their skulls are removed, cleaned, and installed among the voidship’s shrines and ossuaries.
It is terrible luck to make an important decision while the ship is not being bathed in starlight.
As thy shift begins, anoint thyself with the oils used in thy shipbound station.
Faith is the greatest shield. When the voidship travels through the Warp, someone must always be praying; the crew take overlapping duty shifts to ensure this happens.
Spirit of Navigation: The machine spirit of this vehicle can unerringly align itself with the magnetic field of the world, providing better guidance through unusual weather or interference.
Resplendent: This vehicle is highly resistant to dirt, grime, and filth of any kind. With a quick chem-scour, it gleams as if freshly manufactured.
Protective: When a Crew or Passenger of this vehicle suffers Damage as a result of a Critical Hit or Out of Control, they reduce that Damage by 1, (minimum of 1).
Quick Fix: This vehicle responds quickly to emergency or thorough repairs and seems almost eager to return to action. (Narratively or mechanically lowers how long repairs take).

Daring: The machine spirit of this vehicle displays a strange willingness to perform risky manoeuvres. (The driver gets +1 SL on performing @UUID[JournalEntry.fpiV4F49v3gxmipn.JournalEntryPage.E6ehBMkpK3H21CpO]{Vehicle Actions}).

Quicksilver Machine: When this vehicle is used to perform the @UUID[JournalEntry.fpiV4F49v3gxmipn.JournalEntryPage.E6ehBMkpK3H21CpO#evasive-manoeuvres]{Evasive Manoeuvres} Vehicle Action, the Difficulty of the action gets easier by one step.

Meteoric Impact: This vehicle’s machine spirit drives it to strike enemies with a vengeance. When performing the @UUID[JournalEntry.fpiV4F49v3gxmipn.JournalEntryPage.E6ehBMkpK3H21CpO#ram]{Ram} Vehicle Action, treat this vehicle’s Size as one step higher for the purposes of Damage.
Hunter: The machine spirit of his vehicle relishes a chase. Once per encounter, the driver gains +1 SL when making a Piloting Test to pursue another vehicle.
Steady Machine: This vehicle is almost unnaturally well-stabilised, such that all crew and passengers have an easy time embarking and disembarking.
Bulwark: When this vehicle rolls on a Critical Hit Table, reduce the result by 1, to a minimum of 1.
Broken Road: A rockside or fallen masonry has covered the road. Some explosives or hard work could clear the debris, but it could cause a lot of noise and draw the attention of others.
Overgrown/Overpopulated Area: The vehicle needs to move through a densely overgrown or overpopulated area. What are they going to do to clear the way?
Enemy Ambush/Checkpoint: The enemy has set up an ambush, using broken vehicles and barricades to box in oncoming vehicles. Do the characters notice in time? Can they trick their way through?

Extreme Weather/Condition: Heavy rain or snowfall buffets the area, or is mired in radioactive fallout or noxious gases. Characters should stay inside, and visibility is severely reduced (Hazard or Obscured).
Long Bridge: The landscape presents a deep gorge; the only way across is over a narrow bridge. A battle or disaster happened here, and the bridge looks unstable.
Enemy Patrol: Some enemies appear, riding a band of smaller fast vehicles. The characters have just enough time to hide, or do they take the opportunity to strike first? Fight or Flight?

Minefield: The expanse in front of them is covered in wrecked vehicles and craters; mines have been placed here. Do the characters take time to cross the minefield carefully, or take the long way around?

Survivors: The characters encounter a group of survivors. They all seek aid, showing deep desperation in their eyes. Can the characters trust them? Can they afford to lend aid? It might jeopardise the mission.
Sniper/Lookout: In the distance, a sniper starts taking pot-shots at the vehicle and crew. Do they attempt to fight back or flee the area? They might report the party’s position to others.
Long Tunnel: The road leads to a long tunnel or deep dark gorge. The entire area within is Dark, the terrain is unknown, and anything could be lurking inside.

Blinding Warp Storm: The Warp broils with energy, and the navigator shrieks that they cannot see the Astronomican. The captain orders an emergency return to realspace, emerging in an unknown location.

Daemonic Manifestation: The Geller Field is breached, and coruscating psychic energy surges through the decks, looping and warping into the manifestation of @UUID[Compendium.apex-imperialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.6hX0E9XlPUoRaDaQ.JournalEntryPage.O9kga3ngGfFyIsze]{daemons}.
Crew Possession: A wave of daemonic energy lashes against the voidship, allowing daemons to enter the minds of some aboard, puppeteering their bodies to frenzied mutiny.
Echoing Whispers: Hushed voices ring through vox systems and inside the crew’s minds, telling of past horrors and worse things yet to come. All aboard must succeed at a Discipline Test or be Stunned.
Seeping Corruption: Daemonic growths start to sprout between the decks. Panels are burst open by writhing flesh, dotted with staring eyes and reeking of rot.
Ruin of the Faithful: Holy symbols aboard the voidship shatter, tarnish, or melt while ringing with the laughter of four voices. None dare speculate on the sound’s source.
Writhing Horror: An amorphous mass of mouth and tentacle pushes through the Geller Field and latches onto the voidship’s hull, clanging against it as the Geller Field slowly kills it.

Psychic Pulse: The Geller Field crackles as a pulse of psychic energy forces all psykers aboard to succeed at a Psychic Mastery Test or roll on the @UUID[Compendium.apex-imperialis.navis-core-tables.RollTable.9aSbu2mswOOI43J1]{Psychic Phenomena} Table.

Twisting Infinity: The fabric of the Warp contracts and bulges, shortening or extending the voidship’s journey, as the distance of a week’s passage is compressed to a few hours or stretched into months.
Haemorrhaging Hull: With a groaning of metal, rivulets of thick, dark blood begin to pour down the walls of the voidship, pooling into slick rivers that run through the ship.
Shadow in the Warp: The voidship passes into a region of inexplicable silence, the navigator straining to see the Astronomican and all the crew feeling a deep dread that only comes from being hunted.
Warp Leviathan: An unfathomably large creature comes into view of the voidship’s scanners, moving parallel to the vessel as if riding the wake of the Geller Field.
Steel to Flesh: The crew’s vision flickers between the voidship in its normal form, and a twisted version of the vessel, its entire hull made from writhing flesh.
Twisted Taste: The energies of the Warp confuse electrochemical signals, every sensory input gaining a flavour — the sound of the engines, the colour of the uniforms, the shaking of the voidship.
Spectral Hounds: The halls ring with running claws and distant howling, though no physical presence can be detected. Animals aboard the voidship bolt for cover or die of terror on the spot.
Inverted Vision: Psychic energy batters the Geller Field, warping the vision of those aboard in pulsing waves of inverted colours, save for those lucky enough to bear augmetic eyes.
Ghost Ship: The voidship’s scanners detect another vessel alongside it, but no communication can be made with it, and no vessel can be seen by those who look through viewports.
Unreal Glow: The energies of the Warp imbue parts of the deck with a lambent aura of shifting colours that fade once the voidship emerges from the Warp.
Unnerving Charge: A static charge is cast over the voidship, and the crew hesitates to touch controls and apparatus unnecessarily to avoid the pain of sharp electric cracks.
Geller Flicker: The voidship shudders as its Geller Field flickers. Tendrils of the Warp reach towards the vessel but are cut off as the field surges back to life.

Control Test: Challenging (+0) if the driver was hit

The Cargo compartment, if there is one, is struck. The results are up to the GM — the cargo might be damaged, or some of it might spill out from the vehicle. If there is no cargo, treat this as a Crew/Passengers Hit result instead.

Control Test: Routine (+20)

A randomly chosen weapon is damaged, and will not function again until repaired. A second result on the same weapon destroys it completely. If the vehicle has no weapons, or they have all been destroyed, treat this as a Crew/Passengers Hit result instead.

Control Test: Routine (+20)

Reduce the vehicle’s Armour by [[/r 1d5]] on either its front or side, as appropriate for the attack which caused this result. Control Test: Challenging (+0)

The vehicle suffers a hit to a wing or engine. If the Speed would be reduced below Slow, the vehicle is @UUID[JournalEntry.fpiV4F49v3gxmipn.JournalEntryPage.I4mFYORL990yUAjB#out-of-control]{Out Of Control}.

Control Test: Difficult (-10)

The vehicle is destroyed outright, falling to the ground in a blazing inferno. Everyone inside takes [[/r 1d10 + 10 # Damage]] Damage to a random Hit Location and suffers the@UUID[Compendium.apex-imperialis.navis-core-journals.JournalEntry.DjxnvYJajGflu7IY.JournalEntryPage.Tu0sU1bo9eZI6qoe#ablaze]{Ablaze} Condition.

Curtailed: Each encounter, until you take the Aim Action with this weapon, its effective Range is lowered by one step.
Drained Spirit: Once per encounter, the first time you would score a Critical Hit with this weapon, it is treated as a normal successful hit.

Surrounded: Once per encounter, the first time you use this weapon while Outnumbered, you must roll on the @UUID[Compendium.apex-imperialis.navis-core-tables.RollTable.HL6DtTGWIUQy5NZ9]{Fumble} Table.

Condemn: When you Burn Fate, the next time you make an attack with this weapon, you must roll on the Fumble Table.
Odious Spirit: Once per encounter, the first time you make an attack with this weapon and you have a Mutation or Malignancy, you make the Test with Disadvantage.
Nyctophobia: The first time in an encounter you make an Attack with this weapon while in a Dark, Obscured, or Poorly Lit environment, you must roll on the Fumble Table.

The hilt of a broken blade, wielded by a relative who fell in Astra Militarum service

Unsullied: This armour always smells clean, and cannot be permanently stained or tainted by any kind of filth.
Buoyant: Despite the weight of this armour or anything else one might carry, some quirk of its design makes it easy to stay afloat in liquids, and even aid in swimming.
Quick Catches: Through clever design, or some unknown modification, this armour is easy to don and easy to get out of. It takes half as much time to don or doff this armour.
Celerity: Once per encounter, while you have 1 or more Superiority and wearing this armour, your Speed is Fast for the duration of a turn.
Defiant Grit: Once per encounter, when your party has no Superiority and you suffer a Critical Hit, reduce the roll on the Critical Wounds Table by 1.
Unscoured: Once per encounter, while your party has 1 or more Superiority, the first time you would be afflicted by the Ablaze Condition, you instead ignore it.
Instinct Spirit: Once per encounter, you gain +1 SL when making a Reflexes (Dodge) Test to avoid Blast or Spread weapons.
Domineering: The armour’s adornments make it particularly terrorising to some. While wearing it, once per encounter, you gain +1 SL on a Presence (Intimidation) Test.
Fortified: Once per encounter, if you receive a Critical Hit while benefiting from any kind of Cover, reduce the roll on the Critical Wounds Table by 1.
Righteous Bulwark: Once per encounter, if you receive a Critical Hit while you are Defending a Zone in combat, reduce the roll on the Critical Wounds Table by 1.
Deceptive: Through an unusual manufactorum design or pattern, this piece of equipment looks like a similar piece of equipment and might be deceptive in expectations.
Enduring: If this item has a duration, it is doubled, otherwise this item is particularly resistant to bumps and scrapes that might wear it down or damage it.
Comfortable Fit: You are so accustomed to the item that it becomes easier to bear, reduce the Enc of the item by 1.
Emblematic: This item aptly personifies a function of an Imperium Faction, and garners a positive disposition when interacting with members of that Faction.
Exemplar: If this item has an associated Test, or the GM asks for a Test as part of its function, once per encounter gain +1 SL to that Test.
Reticent: This item or piece of equipment functions quieter than other, similar items. Even in use, it might be possible to avoid attention or otherwise not attract notice while using it.
Emboldening: Once per encounter, the presence of this item empowers your resolve and inspires your faith in the Imperium, adding +1 SL to any Discipline Test.
Expeditious: This item or piece of equipment performs its function rapidly and often eagerly.
Unblemished: This item or piece of equipment is easy to clean, rejects dirt and filth, and resists all manner of toxins or contaminants that it might otherwise carry.
Hallowed: Through damage, scrapes, or repairs, this item has taken on a strange countenance to an item of faith, and now functions as a Holy Symbol for the bearer.
Unsettling Sonics: The engines or mechanisms of this vehicle are louder than normal, and crew or passengers complain about barely audible howling that accompanies it, straining the mind.
Selfish Preservation: When this vehicle suffers a Critical Hit, on a result of Cargo Hit or Weapon Hit, roll [[/r d10]]. On a 6+, the result becomes Crew/Passengers Hit.
Squalid Machine: This vehicle is difficult to keep clean, and carries with it all manner of filth and contaminants from the zones and battlefields it frequents.

Abhorrent Enemy: The machine spirit of this vehicle abhors one enemy of the Imperium: daemonic, Infractionist, mutant, or xenos. The vehicle worsens any attempt to get close to such a vehicle or enemy by 10.
Tomb Vehicle: When a Crew or Passenger of this vehicle suffers Damage due to a Critical Hit or Out of Control, they increase that Damage by 1.
Trundling: Once per day, this vehicle will refuse to move faster than a Slow Speed during its first turn.

Withdraw: When this vehicle suffers a Critical Hit, on its next turn, the driver must make a Challenging (+0) Piloting Test or the vehicle immediately makes the @UUID[JournalEntry.fpiV4F49v3gxmipn.JournalEntryPage.E6ehBMkpK3H21CpO#evasive-manoeuvres]{Evasive Manoeuvres} Vehicle Action.
Scarred: This vehicle bears its damage poorly and takes longer to repair than normal vehicles (narratively or mechanically, making it longer to repair sufficiently).

Wrathful: The machine spirit of this vehicle abhors trickery or evasiveness, especially when confronted with enemies. The Difficulty of @UUID[JournalEntry.fpiV4F49v3gxmipn.JournalEntryPage.E6ehBMkpK3H21CpO#evasive-manoeuvres]{Evasive Manoeuvres} gets harder by one step.
Appeasement: The vehicle will refuse to start quickly and demands an unusual and thorough ritual to appease it.
Warp Storm: A sudden Warp storm manifests before the vessel can change course. Roll on the @UUID[RollTable.dAiKbA0EKMtz9Ozl]{Warp Encounter Table} as the crew scrambles to activate the Geller Field.
Space Hulk: The scanners indicate an unfathomably large vessel emerging from the Warp — a space hulk, an amalgamation of millennia of void wreckage containing all manner of Warp-spawned horrors.

Solar Flare: A lash of radioactive flame signals an electromagnetic particle ejection from the nearest star that disables the voidship for some time; the decks are plunged into darkness, lit by scant emergency lighting.

Ork Freebooterz: The hull rattles with a hail of crude heavy calibre shells as Ork voidfighters emerge from behind a cluster of asteroids. It begins to make strafing runs in an incredibly loose formation.
Inquisitorial Corvette: A vessel that lacks the baroque decoration of typical Imperial vessels comes into physical view. No lights glow from its black hull, and scanners do not detect it.
Aeldari Corsairs: A sleek xenos vessel is detected tailing the voidship, out of range of its weaponry. If records of past engagements are to be believed, more will soon follow.
Human Pirates: Unknown vessels appear on the scanners. Vox calls to identify themselves are responded to with an ultimatum: ‘Surrender your cargo willingly, or it will be taken by force.’

Inhabited Derelict: A drifting, damaged vessel, although scanners show some signs of life within. Such vessels are often dens for xenos horrors the likes of @UUID[Compendium.apex-imperialis.navis-core-actors.Actor.KvLrPAQ0gmIWSvfX]{Purestrain Genestealers}
Listening Post: A small void station monitors the surrounding stretch of this subsector and all passing void traffic. Unexpected vessels are boarded, and their cargo is inspected.
Rogue Trader: A sleek yet sturdy vessel built for plying the edges of known space. It returns from such a voyage with records of newly explored worlds at the sector’s edge.
Drifting Wreckage: A fractured husk of a voidship comes up on the scanners; a field of debris and the bodies of its crew are strewn across the vacuum of the void.
Void Parasite: A xenos life form clinging to the voidship’s exterior has been detected. It must be destroyed before it can threaten the integrity of the hull.
Distress Beacon: A static-laden call is received from a nearby vessel, void station, or asteroid colony. Their condition is unknown; their comms array is damaged, and they seek assistance.
Imperial Navy Blockade: Mighty Lunar-class cruisers of the Imperial Fleet are en route to a nearby planet. Vox messages order incoming vessels to alter course or be destroyed.
Asteroid Field: The void ahead is littered with drifting rock, some of the bodies no larger than a Human, while others dwarf the voidship entirely. Passage demands precise navigation.
Escape Pod: The ship’s scanners alert the crew to a nearby escape pod, with vitals indicating a single living passenger. They alone know the grim fate of their vessel.
Pilgrim Vessel: The debris of the void has chipped away at reliefs of saints and prayers engraved in its hull, but no awe is lost to those travelling aboard it.
Cosmic Dust: A haze of cosmic dust obscures vision from the windows and viewports. Vox channels are preoccupied with coordinating any small vessels in the fog-like phenomenon.
Meteoroid Hail: The void shields glitter as a shower of tiny celestial bodies disintegrate on impact. Any nearby small vessels without void shields are battered and punctured.
Freighter: A chartered merchant vessel bears the fruits of a forge world through the void to colony or warzone, its hull scarred from centuries of remarkable yet unremembered service.
A dagger carved from stone chipped off a void kraken that almost devoured your ship a century ago (@UUID[Compendium.apex-imperialis.navis-core-items.Item.qQ8Y8nmiaTaKgzvs]{Knife})
A @UUID[Compendium.apex-imperialis.navis-core-items.Item.oaY0wS7LewD6DXK6]{Holy Icon} made of bent wire and scrap, beseeching voidship machine spirits to guard against decompression

A pair of Bulky @UUID[Compendium.apex-imperialis.navis-core-items.Item.OjLq7yDUPG8TpISi]{Choke Grenades}, jury-rigged from fire suppressants during an attempted mutiny

rows.text: A Human captive hangs from a rope in a dead-end tunnel. They’re still alive, kicking and cursing, trying to get free. If the characters release them, they attack the party with nothing but their elongated teeth and nails. They’ve already been touched by Chaos, infused with manic strength (use the @UUID[Compendium.apex-imperialis.navis-core-actors.Actor.qBvBctGcZoWcW7Tz]{Manufactorum Labourer} stat-block to represent them, but increase their strength by 15 and they have the following attack — Tooth and Nail: Melee (Brawling) 40, 1 + SL difference Damage. Penetrating (4).

A mutated captive, consumed by rage and madness, roams the tunnels, a victim of the Shaman’s rites (Use the @UUID[Compendium.apex-imperialis.navis-core-actors.Actor.utelXH1DahFI5iHt]{Accursed Cultist} stat-block to represent them).

@UUID[Actor.J8fomG1IJs18g3F5]{Gelka} steps into the party’s path, brandishing twin hammers, and challenges the characters, seeking to discover their intentions. She intends to kill the Shaman and release her herd from his influence — the characters might consider her a potential ally.

A partially collapsed tunnel has been turned into a profane shrine. Scraps of flesh and bloodied clothes have been pushed between cracks in broken stones, and marks have been scratched on the walls using blood, ash, or other means. There seems to be no one here, but if the party investigates too closely, a @UUID[Actor.TRcwwntLPqt7KaJy]{Mutated Beastman} surprises them from behind.

A @UUID[Actor.ri94quNUXFjXfjI3]{Beastman} has fallen foul of the ravages of Chaos and become a @UUID[Compendium.apex-imperialis.navis-core-actors.Actor.7GvkaaVAd69ORno0]{Chaos Spawn}. This creature bleats and screams as it passes through the tunnels, so the party should be able to avoid its path. It has no eyes, but if it hears them, it pursues relentlessly and attacks.

A group of @UUID[Actor.ri94quNUXFjXfjI3]{Beastmen} (a number equal to party size) led by a @UUID[Actor.TRcwwntLPqt7KaJy]{Mutated Beastman} carrying a flaming torch patrols the tunnels. They are looking for intruders, and if any of the Beastmen detect the party, the entire patrol attacks at once.
‘A voice calls your name, and each time it repeats, it sounds deeper, wetter, and less human.’
‘The barking laughter of a dozen voices seems to come from inside a nearby wall.’
‘You hear a child’s voice call out to you from a nearby drain, saying ‘Help me’.’
‘Scratching seems to follow you, like the sound of clawed fingers raking repeatedly across rusted deck plates.’
‘A wet slithering sound, like something smooth wriggling through mud, terminates in an echo of inhuman footsteps.’
‘A faint babbling seems to intermingle with the sound of running water, soon you realise it’s not babbling, it’s weeping.’
‘A loud thumping noise catches your attention from somewhere far off, gradually building faster and faster.’
‘You hear a whispered voice repeating the same phrase, it takes you a moment to realise it's saying… ‘Soon they’ll know’.’
‘A scream cuts through the air raw and blood curdling, echoing out around you in a cacophony of suffering.’
‘Heavy footsteps thunder like heavy cannon fire, slowly drawing closer and closer until they seem all around you.’

A spray of especially caustic chemicals splashes across a random hit location, destroying up to 3 points of armour on that location. If the hit location is unarmoured, then flesh is stripped to the bone, inflicting [[/r 1d10]] Damage on that location instead.

The Rejuvenat precursors inflict a gradual detrimental effect on your tissue, adding [[/r 2d10]] to your apparent age over the next week.
You suffer a hideous mutation! At the end of the encounter, roll on the @UUID[Compendium.apex-imperialis.navis-core-tables.RollTable.aHz4wSCM8ogTVOhT]{Mutations Table}.

This particular mix of Rejuvenat seems to have some effect. At the end of the encounter, you gain the @UUID[Compendium.apex-imperialis.navis-core-items.Item.gLYbTQPGuxwSPURo]{Inhuman Beauty} Mutation.

Markis Sihn is a saviour to the people. He heals citizens who become sick from the chemical manufactorum’s by-products in the region, and he asks little in return. [True, discounting the fact that those he heals are also transformed.]
Sihn is, in fact, a xenos entity that has come to punish local citizens of the Imperium. Some more informed characters may press the point that he’s an Aeldari wych. [False, on both accounts.]
A group of mercenaries were just asking about Sihn. I didn’t get too good a look at them but… (You should pick one of the other hunting teams and describe someone memorable among them.) [True.]

In region Gamma-74, a Stilt-fleet walker was attacked by a massive beast; Markis Sihn called the beast out of the wastes with his strange powers. [Partially true. A walker was attacked, but it was by marauders, not by a beast. Rumours about a beast was started by @UUID[Actor.siMMykRHCMATkA9u]{Rastigan Dorin}.]

The workers in the acid refineries, processing plants, and crawlers of Gamma-74 have had enough. They are sick and tired of being sick and tired. Sihn showed them there is another way. That they do not have to waste their lives for others. [Partially true. Sihn inspired the workers to join his cult but wanted nothing to do with any rebellion.]

Manufactorum 74-c15 has been shut down. People say it was rioting workers, but I know the truth: it was Ork raiders! Don’t go outside without a rebreather or some filtration plugs; the acid in the air will eat through your lungs from the first breath.
I heard massive beasts are lurking in the world’s wastes, some as big as an Imperial Knight. You won’t see them until they surface and strike.
They wash the mid levels of their hives with the same acid they harvest; artificial rain to keep it all clean. Keep an eye on the Adeptus Administratum’s cleansing procedures to avoid getting burned.
Make sure you’ve got paperwork for your weapons if you’re going into the Upper Hives. The Vigilites are always looking for an excuse to lock people up.
Don’t get caught doing anything you shouldn’t near Hive Sanksorak, or mess too much with House Vylathi — they’ll take any reason to bolster their penal legion.
Never eat uncured acynadi meat; the tinned stuff is fine, but if it’s unprocessed, you’ll be emptying your bowels for days, and you might not have any bowels left afterwards.
Walkers are the best means to travel across Voll’s uneven wastes. Any boat would get its hull eaten through in a couple of days, and you don’t want to sink into a swamp that’ll eat your skin off.

Gangs are everywhere, but it’s the guilds you’ve got to keep your eyes on. The Mercator Carnem, Mercator Dilaquo, and Mercator Lenimen — food, water, and chems, respectively. A ganger might take your life, but the guilds can make your life not worth living.

The highborn symbolically scar their flesh off the acid rain by stepping out bare-headed onto their balconies when it’s raining. Some do it as a cleansing ritual, but others see it as a mark of privilege and status, a gift from living atop uncovered towers.
